scope: Drawing payloads only, between LaTeX passes of a freshly prepared build. Code outside pictures, pre/post hooks and listings always execute.
review: Luna agents inspected sources for side effects and dependencies. Unflagged examples are not proven pure. Only exact source matches with eligible status may use the cache; changed files lose eligibility until reviewed again.

examples.reason: This executed example allocates a new dimension register with \newdimen. Register allocation is global TeX state and is not undone by the codeexample group; replaying on every pass allocates again, while skipping it can change allocation order for later code.

Rendered plot output depends on external plotdata files. Source-only result reuse can return stale artwork when the files differ between builds/passes.
Both table rendering and plot rendering depend on an external data file; cache validity must include that file's contents/identity.

This executed plot writes three plot-label records to LaTeX auxiliary state and samples unseeded rand. A cache hit that skips the body can omit/reorder label writes and leaves the PGF random stream at a different position for later examples.

legend to name=named exports a legend through label/auxiliary machinery; the following \ref{named} depends on the aux record and saved legend payload from this example. Reusing only rendered output must preserve/replay that state.
Plot expression `{rand}` generates random samples and consumes PGF random state.

First picture plots `rnd` and saves a named colorbar `storedcolorbar`; subsequent pictures reuse that named colorbar. Reusing only rendered picture output can omit both RNG consumption and the named picture production needed downstream.
Two plot expressions use `rand`; both consume random state and produce pass/build-dependent geometry.
The example explicitly seeds and consumes the PGF random stream. Skipping it changes the state observed by later random plots (even though this plot is reproducible in isolation).
Scatter coordinates `(rand,rand)` consume two random draws per sample; result depends on RNG state.
